---
title: "Shared, private and separate libraries"
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Shared, private and separate libraries}
  %\VignetteEngine{quarto::html}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

By default, `install_library()` compiles every installed client into one shared
library. All clients in a library share one Julia environment, so when their
`[compat]` bounds conflict, the build leaves the later ones out (see [When
clients conflict](using-clients.html#when-clients-conflict)). Such a client can
instead get a private library of its own, or go into a separate library that you
select for the R sessions that use it. This vignette compares the three.

  |                        | [Shared](#the-shared-library) | [Private](#private-libraries)       | [Separate](#separate-libraries)        |
  | ---------------------- | ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------  | -------------------------------------- |
  | Set up with            | `install_library()`           | `install_library(private = "pkg")`  | `build_library()` and `JLBIND_LIBRARY` |
  | Clients in one session | Those in the library          | All                                 | Those in the selected library          |
  | Disk space overhead    | 2 MB                          | 27–60 MB or more per private client | 2 MB per library                       |
  | Julia runtimes         | One                           | One per library                     | One                                    |
  | Rebuilt by             | `install_library()`           | `install_library()`                 | You                                    |
  | Systems                | All                           | All[^windows]                       | All                                    |

The overhead comes on top of each client's compiled code, which every layout
holds (about 9 MB for CausalStructures.jl; see [Bundle
sizes](build-options.html#bundle-sizes)). A private library's copy of the
runtime is larger on Windows (60 MB) than on Linux (27 MB), and grows with the
standard libraries its dependencies use: a private library of
CausalStructures.jl, whose dependencies need OpenBLAS, is 88 MB on Linux and 116
MB on Windows. With private or separate libraries, a dependency that several
clients share is compiled into each of their libraries. Thus, we recommend you
to use the default with shared libraries, unless impossible due to conflicts.

## The shared library

`install_library()` stores the shared library under
`tools::R_user_dir("jlbind", "cache")` and rebuilds it whenever a client or the
Julia version changes. It uses the runtime of the Julia that built it, so it is
small, and all clients share one Julia heap, one set of
[threads](using-clients.html#threads) and each other's [Julia
objects](technical-details.html#julia-objects-in-r). Each build compiles every
client, and a client that conflicts with those before it is left out. To choose
which clients to build it from, and in which order to resolve them, name them:

```r
jlbind::install_library(packages = c("pkgA", "pkgC"))
```

## Private libraries

A client can get a library of its own:

```r
jlbind::install_library(private = "pkgB")
```

[^windows]: Released JuliaC gives a library a private Julia runtime on Linux and
    macOS. On Windows, that needs the JuliaC of
    [JuliaC.jl#151](https://github.com/JuliaLang/JuliaC.jl/pull/151), not yet
    released; to build with it, set `JLBIND_JULIAC` first:
    `Sys.setenv(JLBIND_JULIAC = "https://github.com/asinghvi17/JuliaC.jl#as/windows-privatize")`.
    Pre-built libraries for Windows are built with it.

This builds the shared library from the other clients, and a library for `pkgB`
with its dependencies resolved for it alone. The private library has its own
copy of the Julia runtime, with its symbols renamed (JuliaC's `--privatize`), so
it loads alongside the shared library and any other private ones, and `pkgB`
works in the same R session as the clients it conflicts with. Later builds keep
it, so `install_library()` rebuilds both. To put every client back into the
shared library, pass `private = character()`.

The runtime copy makes the library a
[bundle](build-options.html#bundled-runtimes), so it runs without Julia
installed. It takes disk space, and in each session its own memory and
`JULIA_NUM_THREADS` threads. Julia objects that `pkgB` returns work with the
functions of `pkgB` only.

A [pre-built library](using-clients.html#pre-built-libraries), installed with
`install_library(method = "download")`, is a private library too, compiled for
any CPU. Later builds leave it alone unless you name its package in `packages`.

## Separate libraries

Clients used in different R sessions can each have a library, built with
`build_library()`:

```r
jlbind::build_library("pkgA", "~/jlbind/pkgA")
jlbind::build_library(c("pkgB", "pkgC"), "~/jlbind/pkgBC")
```

Set `JLBIND_LIBRARY` before the first client loads to select the library for a
session, or in a project's `.Renviron` for every session in that project:

```r
# jlbind.dll on Windows, jlbind.dylib on macOS
Sys.setenv(JLBIND_LIBRARY = "~/jlbind/pkgA/jlbind.so")
library(pkgA)
```

Every client in that session then binds to this library, in place of the shared
and private ones. A separate library is as small as the shared one, but you
rebuild it yourself: after updating one of its clients, run `build_library()`
again (`check_bound()` reports when it's needed).
